title: Identification of Different EEC Types and Nerve Fiber Types in Human Gastric Mucosa
author: Madeleine Di Natale
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8u7hwzn

steps.title: Collect gastric tissue from patients
steps.instruction: Obtain stomach tissue from patients undergoing gastric sleeve surgery at the Renown Regional Medical Center, Reno, Nevada.

steps.title: Place tissue in cold PBS
steps.instruction: Immediately immerse the excised tissue in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS: 0.15 M NaCl in 0.01 M sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.2) kept on ice.

steps.title: Dissect tissue on ice
steps.instruction: Transfer the iced tissue to the laboratory and dissect it in ice‑cold PBS within 1 hour of retrieval.

steps.title: Fix tissue overnight
steps.instruction: Place dissected pieces in cold fixative (2 % formaldehyde + 0.2 % picric acid in 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0) and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash tissue with DMSO and PBS
steps.instruction: Wash the fixed tissue three times for 10 min each with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), then three times for 10 min each with PBS.

steps.title: Store tissue in PBS‑azide
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue to PBS containing 0.1 % sodium azide (PBS‑azide) and keep at 4 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Cryoprotect and embed tissue
steps.instruction: Trim the tissue block to approximately 1 cm wide, then place it overnight in PBS‑sucrose‑azide (PBS with 30 % sucrose and 0.1 % azide). The next night, transfer to a 1:1 mixture of 50 % PBS‑sucrose‑azide and 50 % OCT (Tissue‑Tek). Finally, embed in 100 % OCT, trim, and freeze in isopentane cooled with liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Embed in 100 % OCT and freeze in isopentane chilled with liquid nitrogen

steps.title: Section tissue at 12 µm
steps.instruction: Cut 12 µm thick sections, place them on SuperFrostPlus® slides (Grale Scientific, Vic, Australia), and let dry at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Block sections with serum/Triton
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in 10 % normal horse serum plus 1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Apply primary antibodies overnight
steps.instruction: Prepare mixtures of primary antibodies for double staining, apply to the blocked sections, and incubate at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Wash sections in PBS
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times with PBS.

steps.title: Incubate with Alexa Fluor secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with appropriate Alexa Fluor‑conjugated secondary antibodies for 1.5 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash and mount sections
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times with PBS, then mount them using non‑fluorescent mounting medium (Dako, Carpinteria, CA, USA).

steps.title: Run negative control without primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Process parallel sections that receive no primary antibodies to assess background staining and autofluorescence.

steps.title: Acquire confocal tile scans
steps.instruction: Using a Zeiss LSM800 confocal microscope with a 20× objective, acquire tile scans of each section for later analysis.

steps.title: Analyze images for fiber density
steps.instruction: Export tile scans, threshold each image to create a mask of immunoreactivity, overlay an offset grid of 13.5 µm‑diameter circles spaced ~38 µm apart, count circles intersecting immunoreactivity, and calculate the percentage of positive sampling areas within the muscle regions of the corpus. Repeat this analysis for tissues from four patients.

substeps.instruction: Export and threshold images to generate masks
Place 13.5 µm circles (≈38 µm centre spacing) over each mask
Mark circles with immunoreactivity as positive
Compute % positive circles relative to total circles in corpus muscle

steps.title: Determine co‑bundling/co‑localisation of fibers
steps.instruction: Using a Zeiss AxioImager microscope with a 40× objective, select a region in the first fluorescence channel, count visible fibers, then examine the second channel to classify each fiber as co‑bundled, co‑localised, or single‑labelled. Analyze 25 fields first with the 488 nm channel then the 555 nm channel, and another 25 fields first with the 555 nm channel then the 488 nm channel; calculate percentages of each category and repeat for four patients.

substeps.instruction: In channel 1, count total visible fibers in a selected region
In channel 2, classify each fiber as co‑bundled, co‑localised, or single‑labelled
Calculate percentages of co‑bundled and co‑localised fibers
Repeat analysis for four patient samples
